contributions.statement: Do not let an agent implement from a long chat; start implementation only from a reviewed brief that names non-goals, affected modules, acceptance checks, and the commands to rerun.
contributions.evidence: §VII-B states the rule and §XII question 1 lists brief-versus-chat as future work. No team, repo, or success rate is measured in this paper. Tables I and II specify the brief and the risk tiers without an outcome.
relative_to: 2608.30572 introducing spec-driven development with coding agents

contributions.statement: Keep repository instruction files short and tied to a command the agent will actually run, because the studies this paper cites disagree on whether extra context files help or raise cost and cut success.
contributions.evidence: §II-C cites one AGENTS.md result with lower runtime and tokens, one result where extra context files reduced success and raised cost, and a factorial study with little adherence effect. This paper does not recompute those tables. §X-A repeats the short-file recommendation.
relative_to: 2607.27250 AGENTS.md did not change correctness; the observed effect was fewer blind full-suite runs when the file carried an operational warning

reason: SCOPE-V and the risk tiers are an untested rename of a brief, a V-model, and a human gate. The mixed instruction-file point is already measured elsewhere, and the conversation-to-brief rule is the team's existing spec-first practice stated again without a new result.
